name: Fleece-Crown
geological_features: Thick white ammonia cloud crown at the poles
Rocky core estimated at 15 Earth masses
specific_features: Brilliant white polar cloud formations resembling a fleece crown
Thirty-seven cataloged moons including four with subsurface oceans
description: Fleece-Crown is one of the largest gas giants in the sector, a massive world whose most distinctive feature is the thick cap of brilliant white ammonia clouds that encircles both poles. These polar cloud formations are dense, textured, and brilliantly reflective, standing out against the darker banded atmosphere like a crown of white fleece atop a dark sphere. The clouds are maintained by unique polar vortex dynamics that concentrate ammonia crystals at high latitudes, creating a persistent feature that has been stable for at least the century and a half since the planet was first observed.

Fleece-Crown's immense gravity dominates its region of space, holding thirty-seven confirmed moons in orbits ranging from near-surface skimmers to distant wanderers at the edge of the planet's gravitational influence. Four of these moons show strong evidence of subsurface liquid water oceans, maintained by tidal heating from the giant planet's gravitational flexing. These moons represent some of the most promising sites for life detection in the outer system, and survey missions are planned or underway for all four.

The planet itself is hostile beyond any reasonable approach distance. Its magnetic field is powerful enough to induce dangerous currents in unshielded spacecraft, and the radiation environment near the planet's equator would deliver lethal doses to an unprotected human within minutes. The atmospheric chemistry includes hydrogen cyanide and other compounds toxic at parts-per-million concentrations, and the pressure at the cloud tops—the shallowest accessible layer—already exceeds one Earth atmosphere. Deeper layers are simply the stuff of physics textbooks, pressures and temperatures that crush matter into exotic states.

Despite the hazards, Fleece-Crown is strategically important as the gravitational anchor for its moon system, which collectively holds more accessible water ice than any other location in the outer system. The four ocean moons are the focus of intense scientific and commercial interest, and a crewed research station orbits the outermost of them, safely beyond the worst of the radiation environment. The fleece crown itself has become a navigational landmark, visible to the naked eye from across the system as a brilliant white point of light, a beacon marking the boundary between the inner and outer reaches.
